## Overview

An earlier analysis of these samples used AOI-level limma models with patient blocking, RUV normalisation and ESTIMATE purity as a covariate. It reported many genes differing between non-responders and responders, a neuroendocrine programme in non-responders and a correlation between a neuroendocrine score and PSMA-PET tumour growth. This script asks whether those findings hold when the patient is the unit of inference.

It (A) reads back the earlier AOI-level gene counts; (B) refits the non-responder versus responder contrast and continuous PSA change in patient pseudobulk on the LOQ gene universe under four covariate sets (none; batch; batch + ESTIMATE purity; batch + deconvolved tumour fraction), including the genes named in the earlier analysis; (C) calibrates the batch and batch + purity models by 200 patient-level label permutations; (D) checks whether purity differs by response and how it relates to deconvolved tumour fraction; and (E) reproduces the neuroendocrine–PET correlation at AOI and patient level and scores neuroendocrine and AR sets with mean z-scores and singscore.

Patient-level purity and tumour fraction are library-size-weighted means over the patient's AOIs, matching the summed-count pseudobulk. Intermediate patients are excluded from the categorical contrast.

**Figures, tables and results supported**

- Extended Data Fig. 8a (genes at FDR < 0.05, earlier AOI-level models versus patient pseudobulk under covariate sets), via comp_28/comp_41
- Extended Data Fig. 9a–c (ESTIMATE purity versus tumour fraction, purity by response, earlier named genes under covariate sets), via comp_28/comp_41
- Extended Data Fig. 10a (pseudobulk counts, via comp_22/comp_24)
- Supplementary Tables 30–34 (via comp_25)
- Results: Re-evaluation of earlier neuroendocrine, purity and bone-niche findings
- Methods: Reconciliation with earlier analyses and the standR workflow

**Pipeline step:** `./run_pipeline.sh --only 18_nepc_purity_reconcile`. Approximate runtime: tens of minutes (200 permutations × 2 covariate sets × 6 strata of limma-voom).

## Analysis

Header listing sections A–E of the re-evaluation.

### Set-up
Loads the AOI object, clinical table, LOQ gene universes and SpatialDecon epithelial-tumour fractions. Defines the genes named in the earlier analysis (`deck_genes`), the literature 13-gene neuroendocrine marker set, the seven neuroendocrine genes the earlier analysis selected on response in these samples (`deck_ne`, kept as a circular reference) and the Hallmark androgen-response set.

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-01}
## ============================================================================
## PRINCE -- R3: reconcile the earlier purity-adjusted NEPC/AR findings
## (PRINCE_GeoMx_Conference_Deck.pptx; phase4_DE.R / phase5_purity_covariate.R /
## phase8_nepc_longitudinal.R) with the patient-level analysis.
##  A. Earlier AOI-level results, read back from Results/Phase4_DE, Phase5_Purity
##  B. Patient-level pseudobulk on the LOQ-filtered gene universe (comp_16), NR vs R
##     (Intermediate excluded) and continuous PSA change, under four covariate sets:
##     none | batch | batch + ESTIMATE purity | batch + deconvolved tumour fraction
##     -> genes at FDR < 0.05 / 0.1, and the deck's named genes
##  C. Permutation calibration: shuffle NR/R labels across patients (200x), refit the
##     purity-adjusted model, count FDR < 0.05 genes -> how often does the observed
##     number arise by chance?
##  D. Purity diagnostics: ESTIMATE purity vs response and vs deconvolved tumour fraction
##  E. NEPC / AR scores vs response and vs PSMA-PET (SUVmean, volume, volume change),
##     at patient level; reproduction of the reported r = 0.38 (PET volume change)
## Outputs: results/R3_nepc_purity/
## ============================================================================

source(file.path(Sys.getenv("PRINCE_ROOT", "."), ".build", "comp_00_guard.R"))
suppressMessages({
  library(qs); library(SummarizedExperiment); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(edgeR); library(limma); library(singscore)
})
setwd(PRINCE_DIR)
check_ram_or_stop(20)
set.seed(2026)
out_dir <- file.path(COMP_DIR, "R3_nepc_purity"); dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

se <- qs::qread("phase2_se_qc_filtered.qs"); cd <- as.data.frame(colData(se))
pt <- qs::qread(out_path("C1_clinical", "patient_table.qs"))
uni <- qs::qread(file.path(COMP_DIR, "R1_loq", "loq_gene_universes.qs"))$universes
dec <- qs::qread(out_path("C3_deconvolution", "deconvolution_proportions.qs"))
tum_frac <- c(dec$lineage_primary[, "Epithelial_tumour"], dec$lineage_bone[, "Epithelial_tumour"])
msig <- readRDS(file.path(PMCC_DIR, "msigdb_gene_sets.rds"))
code <- c("CD45+" = "CD45", "PSMA+" = "PSMA", "PanCK+PSMA-" = "PanCKPSMA")
deck_genes <- c("FOLH1", "TMPRSS2", "KLK2", "KLK3", "NKX3-1", "NEUROD1", "NCAM2", "BEX2", "ID2", "BCOR", "PLXNA3", "STXBP6",
                "CHGA", "SYP", "IBSP", "XRCC2", "B2M", "SSTR5")
nepc13 <- c("ASCL1", "SOX2", "NKX2-1", "FOXA2", "INSM1", "CHGA", "CHGB", "SYP", "NCAM1", "EZH2", "AURKA", "MYCN", "PCSK1")
deck_ne <- c("NEUROD1", "NCAM2", "BEX2", "ID2", "BCOR", "PLXNA3", "STXBP6")
ar_hall <- msig$H$HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE

```

### A. Earlier AOI-level results
Reads the earlier AOI-level toptables (RUV, and RUV + ESTIMATE purity) for pre-treatment and archival strata and records the number of genes at FDR < 0.05 and the FDR of *FOLH1* and *CHGA*. These tables were produced before the bone-only restriction and include lymph-node and soft-tissue biopsies.

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-02}
## ---- A. earlier AOI-level results ---------------------------------------------------------
old <- bind_rows(lapply(c("CD45__Screening", "PSMA__Screening", "PanCKPSMA__Screening", "CD45__Archival", "PSMA__Archival", "PanCKPSMA__Archival"), function(s) {
  a <- read.csv(file.path(PRINCE_DIR, "previous_analysis/Phase4_DE", paste0(s, "_toptable_with_RUV.csv")), row.names = 1)
  b <- read.csv(file.path(PRINCE_DIR, "previous_analysis/Phase5_Purity", paste0(s, "_toptable_with_purity.csv")), row.names = 1)
  data.frame(stratum = s, aoi_RUV_fdr05 = sum(a$adj.P.Val < 0.05), aoi_RUV_purity_fdr05 = sum(b$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
             FOLH1_q_purity = signif(b["FOLH1", "adj.P.Val"], 2), CHGA_q_purity = signif(b["CHGA", "adj.P.Val"], 2))
}))

```

### Patient pseudobulk and model helpers
`pb` sums counts per patient on the stratum's ≥10% LOQ universe, applies TMM and attaches batch, library-size-weighted ESTIMATE purity and tumour fraction, and clinical and PSMA-PET variables. `fit_set` fits limma-voom (robust) for non-responder versus responder (intermediate patients excluded) or PSA change (per 50%), with the requested covariates; aliased columns are dropped by QR pivoting.

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-03}
## ---- pseudobulk builder ---------------------------------------------------------------------
keep_aoi <- cd$response_group_neat != "Control" & cd$timepoint %in% c("Archival", "Screening", "Cycle1")
pb <- function(sg, tp) {
  idx <- which(keep_aoi & cd$segment_name == sg & cd$timepoint == tp); d <- cd[idx, ]
  g <- uni[[paste0(code[sg], "__", tp)]]$g10
  cc <- assay(se, "all_count")[g, idx]
  m <- sapply(split(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$subject_id), function(i) rowSums(cc[, i, drop = FALSE]))
  meta <- d %>% mutate(tf = tum_frac[rownames(d)]) %>% group_by(subject_id) %>%
    summarise(batch = first(study_batch), purity = weighted.mean(tumour.purity.estimate, library_size), tumour_frac = weighted.mean(tf, library_size), n_aoi = n(), .groups = "drop")  # count-weighted, matching summed-count pseudobulk
  meta <- meta[match(colnames(m), meta$subject_id), ] %>%
    left_join(pt %>% select(subject_id, response_group_neat, max_psa_change, psa_change_capped, PSMAPET_BL_SUVmean,
                            PSMAPET_BL_vol, PSMAPET_vol_change_pct), by = "subject_id")
  dge <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(m))
  list(dge = dge, meta = as.data.frame(meta), lcpm = cpm(dge, log = TRUE, prior.count = 1))
}
fit_set <- function(p, contrast, covs) {
  m <- p$meta
  if (contrast == "NR") { keep <- m$response_group_neat %in% c("Responder", "Non_Responder")
    m <- m[keep, ]; dge <- p$dge[, keep]; m$x <- as.integer(m$response_group_neat == "Non_Responder")
  } else { dge <- p$dge; m$x <- m$psa_change_capped / 50 }
  f <- as.formula(paste("~ x", if (length(covs)) paste("+", paste(covs, collapse = " + ")) else ""))
  X <- model.matrix(f, m); X <- X[, qr(X)$pivot[seq_len(qr(X)$rank)], drop = FALSE]
  fit <- eBayes(lmFit(voom(dge, X), X), robust = TRUE)
  topTable(fit, coef = "x", number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
}
covsets <- list(none = character(0), batch = "batch", batch_purity = c("batch", "purity"), batch_tumourfrac = c("batch", "tumour_frac"))

```

### B and C. Covariate sets and permutation calibration
For archival and pre-treatment strata, both contrasts are fitted under the four covariate sets, recording genes at FDR < 0.05 and < 0.1 and the statistics of the earlier named genes. For the batch and batch + purity models, response labels are permuted 200 times among responders and non-responders and the number of FDR < 0.05 genes is recounted; permutation P = (1 + #null ≥ observed)/201.

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-04}
## ---- B + C. pseudobulk DE under covariate sets, with permutation calibration -------------------
de_rows <- list(); gene_rows <- list(); perm_rows <- list()
for (sg in names(code)) for (tp in c("Archival", "Screening")) {
  p <- pb(sg, tp); sid <- paste0(code[sg], "__", tp)
  for (ct in c("NR", "PSA")) for (cs in names(covsets)) {
    tt <- fit_set(p, ct, covsets[[cs]])
    de_rows[[paste(sid, ct, cs)]] <- data.frame(stratum = sid, contrast = ct, covariates = cs,
      n_patients = ifelse(ct == "NR", sum(p$meta$response_group_neat %in% c("Responder", "Non_Responder")), nrow(p$meta)),
      genes = nrow(tt), fdr05 = sum(tt$adj.P.Val < 0.05), fdr10 = sum(tt$adj.P.Val < 0.1))
    g <- intersect(deck_genes, rownames(tt))
    gene_rows[[paste(sid, ct, cs)]] <- data.frame(stratum = sid, contrast = ct, covariates = cs, gene = g,
      logFC = tt[g, "logFC"], P = tt[g, "P.Value"], FDR = tt[g, "adj.P.Val"])
  }
  for (cs in c("batch", "batch_purity")) {
    obs <- de_rows[[paste(sid, "NR", cs)]]$fdr05
    m0 <- p$meta; keep <- m0$response_group_neat %in% c("Responder", "Non_Responder")
    perm <- replicate(200, {
      pp <- p; lab <- m0$response_group_neat; lab[keep] <- sample(lab[keep]); pp$meta$response_group_neat <- lab
      sum(fit_set(pp, "NR", covsets[[cs]])$adj.P.Val < 0.05)
    })
    perm_rows[[paste(sid, cs)]] <- data.frame(stratum = sid, covariates = cs, observed_fdr05 = obs,
      perm_median = median(perm), perm_95pct = quantile(perm, 0.95), perm_p = (1 + sum(perm >= obs)) / 201)
  }
  message(sid, " done")
}
de_tab <- bind_rows(de_rows); gene_tab <- bind_rows(gene_rows); perm_tab <- bind_rows(perm_rows)

```

### D. Purity diagnostics
Per stratum, ESTIMATE purity in non-responders and responders (Wilcoxon), and its Spearman correlation with PSA change and with deconvolved tumour fraction.

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-05}
## ---- D. purity diagnostics -------------------------------------------------------------------
pur <- bind_rows(lapply(names(code), function(sg) bind_rows(lapply(c("Archival", "Screening", "Cycle1"), function(tp) {
  m <- pb(sg, tp)$meta; nrr <- m$response_group_neat %in% c("Responder", "Non_Responder")
  data.frame(stratum = paste0(code[sg], "__", tp), n = nrow(m),
             purity_NR = mean(m$purity[m$response_group_neat == "Non_Responder"]), purity_R = mean(m$purity[m$response_group_neat == "Responder"]),
             p_purity_NR_vs_R = wilcox.test(purity ~ response_group_neat, m[nrr, ], exact = FALSE)$p.value,
             rho_purity_psa = cor(m$purity, m$max_psa_change, method = "spearman"),
             rho_purity_vs_decon = cor(m$purity, m$tumour_frac, method = "spearman"))
}))))

```

### E. Neuroendocrine and AR scores, and PET
- Reproduces the earlier neuroendocrine–PSMA-PET correlation from the earlier per-AOI scores, at patient level (Spearman and Pearson) and with AOIs as observations (pseudoreplicated).
- In patient pseudobulk, scores the detected part of the 13-gene neuroendocrine set, the circular earlier neuroendocrine genes and Hallmark androgen response, as mean z-score and singscore, when at least three genes are detected. Each score is related to PSA change, PSMA-PET volume change and SUVmean (Spearman), and to response group (Wilcoxon; linear model with batch, and with batch + purity).

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-06}
## ---- E. NEPC / AR scores at patient level, and PET ----------------------------------------------
ph8 <- read.csv(file.path(PRINCE_DIR, "previous_analysis/Phase8_NEPC_Longitudinal/all_scores_per_AOI.csv"))
ph8_pt <- ph8 %>% filter(timepoint == "Screening") %>% group_by(subject_id) %>%
  summarise(nepc = mean(score_nepc), ar = mean(score_ar_hallmark), .groups = "drop") %>% left_join(pt, by = "subject_id")
rep_rows <- list()
for (v in c("PSMAPET_vol_change_pct", "PSMAPET_BL_SUVmean", "PSMAPET_BL_vol", "max_psa_change")) {
  ok <- complete.cases(ph8_pt$nepc, ph8_pt[[v]])
  ct <- cor.test(ph8_pt$nepc[ok], ph8_pt[[v]][ok], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
  ctp <- cor.test(ph8_pt$nepc[ok], ph8_pt[[v]][ok], method = "pearson")
  rep_rows[[v]] <- data.frame(score = "Phase 8 NEPC (13 genes, all Screening AOIs, patient mean)", outcome = v,
                              n = sum(ok), spearman = unname(ct$estimate), p_spearman = ct$p.value,
                              pearson = unname(ctp$estimate), p_pearson = ctp$p.value)
}
# AOI-level version (as a deck-style analysis may have used): every Screening AOI as a point
aoi8 <- ph8 %>% filter(timepoint == "Screening") %>% left_join(pt %>% select(subject_id, PSMAPET_vol_change_pct), by = "subject_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(PSMAPET_vol_change_pct))
ct_aoi <- cor.test(aoi8$score_nepc, aoi8$PSMAPET_vol_change_pct, method = "pearson")
rep_rows[["aoi"]] <- data.frame(score = "Phase 8 NEPC, AOI-level (pseudoreplicated)", outcome = "PSMAPET_vol_change_pct",
                                n = nrow(aoi8), spearman = NA, p_spearman = NA, pearson = unname(ct_aoi$estimate), p_pearson = ct_aoi$p.value)

sc_rows <- list()
for (sg in names(code)) for (tp in c("Archival", "Screening")) {
  p <- pb(sg, tp); z <- t(scale(t(p$lcpm))); m <- p$meta
  sets <- list(NEPC13_detected = intersect(nepc13, rownames(z)), deck_NE = intersect(deck_ne, rownames(z)),
               AR_hallmark = intersect(ar_hall, rownames(z)))
  rk <- rankGenes(p$lcpm)
  for (s in names(sets)) {
    g <- sets[[s]]; if (length(g) < 3) next
    sz <- colMeans(z[g, , drop = FALSE]); ss <- simpleScore(rk, upSet = g)$TotalScore
    nrr <- m$response_group_neat %in% c("Responder", "Non_Responder")
    for (meth in c("zmean", "singscore")) {
      y <- if (meth == "zmean") sz else ss
      r <- function(v) { ok <- complete.cases(y, m[[v]]); if (sum(ok) < 8) return(c(NA, NA))
        ct <- cor.test(y[ok], m[[v]][ok], method = "spearman", exact = FALSE); c(ct$estimate, ct$p.value) }
      a <- r("max_psa_change"); b <- r("PSMAPET_vol_change_pct"); cc <- r("PSMAPET_BL_SUVmean")
      fb <- lm(y ~ m$batch); fbp <- lm(y ~ m$batch + m$purity)
      nr <- as.integer(m$response_group_neat == "Non_Responder")
      lmp <- function(form, data) { f <- lm(form, data); s <- summary(f)$coefficients; if ("nr" %in% rownames(s)) s["nr", 4] else NA }
      dd <- data.frame(y = y, nr = nr, batch = m$batch, purity = m$purity)[nrr, ]
      sc_rows[[paste(sg, tp, s, meth)]] <- data.frame(
        stratum = paste0(code[sg], "__", tp), score = s, method = meth, n_genes = length(g), genes = paste(g, collapse = ","),
        n = length(y), n_NR = sum(nr == 1 & nrr), rho_psa = a[1], p_psa = a[2],
        p_NR_wilcox = wilcox.test(y[nrr & nr == 1], y[nrr & nr == 0], exact = FALSE)$p.value,
        p_NR_batch = lmp(y ~ nr + batch, dd), p_NR_batch_purity = lmp(y ~ nr + batch + purity, dd),
        rho_PET_volchange = b[1], p_PET_volchange = b[2], rho_PET_SUVmean = cc[1], p_PET_SUVmean = cc[2])
    }
  }
}
sc_tab <- bind_rows(sc_rows)

```

Prints each section and writes the result tables.

```{r comp-18-nepc-purity-reconcile-07}
## ---- report ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
options(width = 240)
fmt <- function(x) as.data.frame(x %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(.x, 3))))
cat("\n==== A. Earlier AOI-level results (Phase 4 RUV; Phase 5 RUV + purity), NR vs R, FDR < 0.05 ====\n"); print(old, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n==== B. Patient-level pseudobulk (LOQ-filtered genes): genes at FDR < 0.05 / 0.1 ====\n")
print(de_tab %>% pivot_wider(id_cols = c(stratum, contrast, n_patients, genes), names_from = covariates, values_from = c(fdr05, fdr10)) %>% as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n==== C. Permutation calibration (NR vs R, 200 label shuffles) ====\n"); print(fmt(perm_tab), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n==== B. Deck genes, PanCK+PSMA- and PSMA+ Screening, NR vs R ====\n")
print(fmt(gene_tab %>% filter(contrast == "NR", grepl("Screening", stratum), stratum != "CD45__Screening") %>%
  select(stratum, covariates, gene, logFC, P, FDR) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = covariates, values_from = c(logFC, P, FDR))), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n==== D. ESTIMATE purity diagnostics (patient level) ====\n"); print(fmt(pur), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n==== E. Reproducing the NEPC vs PET result ====\n"); print(fmt(bind_rows(rep_rows)), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n==== E. NEPC / NE / AR scores at patient level ====\n"); print(fmt(sc_tab %>% select(-genes)), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(old, file.path(out_dir, "A_earlier_aoi_level_counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(de_tab, file.path(out_dir, "B_pseudobulk_de_by_covariates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(gene_tab, file.path(out_dir, "B_deck_genes_by_covariates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(perm_tab, file.path(out_dir, "C_permutation_calibration.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pur, file.path(out_dir, "D_purity_diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bind_rows(rep_rows), file.path(out_dir, "E_nepc_pet_reproduction.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(sc_tab, file.path(out_dir, "E_scores_patient_level.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nR3 complete.\n")
```
